_provenance: Player-NPC resonance as a measurable physics fact, not a taste judgment. The emitter generates a call (partials); the listener attunes (oscillators). The objective binds the encounter space to the FOUR facts the physicist needs: solvability, the naive trap, the skill gap, and learnability — all worst-cased across K encounters, because the player does not experience the mean.

walls.solvable: The exact inverse MUST be able to silence the call. solvable=0 means too few oscillators for too many partials — the encounter is UNWINNABLE by anyone. This is the anti-frustration gate: the encounter must have a solution at all.
walls.punishes_naive: The ASSUMED strategy (match it directly) MUST be measurably worse than listening. Below 0.10 means 'copy the emitter and hope' works almost as well as actually attuning — the game has no skill curve. The naive player must feel resistance.
walls.skill_gap: Listening MUST outperform flailing by a measurable margin. Below 0.15 means the best listener is barely better than random oscillator settings — the encounter rewards luck, not skill. The gap IS the game: how much better the attentive player does than the button-masher.
walls.headroom: The best listener's residual MUST NOT exceed 70% of the raw call energy. Above 0.70 means even perfect play leaves most of the call uncancelled — the encounter is hopelessly difficult, or the band is too narrow for the partial spread. A game where the best possible outcome is still 70% noise is not fun — it is a punishment.
walls.learnability: Listening MUST pay. learnability is the fraction of call energy a competent listener removes. Below 0.10 means the player gets almost no feedback that they are improving — the energy bar barely moves. The player must SEE their skill register.
walls.assist_hz: The tolerance window MUST stay tight. Above 80 Hz means the assist is so generous that random twiddling converges — the naive player gets rewarded accidentally. The seed started at 40 Hz (deliberately loose); the objective demands it tighten.
